findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that runs the integration tier under --timeout=20 (the equivalent of the unit-tier AC) and reports no unexpected `Failed: Timeout`, proving the step-3 marking sweep is complete before the step-4 CI lowering of _build-and-test.yml:673.
evidence: Context: 'The integration tier is not yet measured.'
Approach 3: 'Measure that tier at --timeout=20, then give each over-budget test @pytest.mark.timeout(N, func_only=True)'
AC only covers default tier: 'python -m pytest -m unit -n 4 ... reports no Failed: Timeout'
Constraint: 'Marking precedes lowering: step 3 before step 4.'
findings.finding: Step 3 (measure the integration tier at --timeout=20 and mark every over-budget test) is the plan's primary open work, but no acceptance criterion verifies it — the only tier-runtime AC exercises the default/unit tier ('measured clean 2026-08-21 at --timeout=20'), while the integration tier is explicitly 'not yet measured'. Step 4 lowers the integration CI lane (_build-and-test.yml:673) to --timeout=20, so an incomplete marking sweep would silently turn integration CI red with no in-plan proving command.
findings.location: Approach step 3 / step 4; Acceptance Criteria (integration tier absent)
scenarios: An integration test exceeds 20s but is left unmarked; step 4 lands and the integration CI lane fails on the next run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: `python -m pytest -m integration ... -q --timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread` reports no `Failed: Timeout` except tests carrying an explicit `@pytest.mark.timeout(N, func_only=True)` with a naming comment.
